papers.finding: Routing algorithm cut the Boston bus fleet 7%; a start-time plan that would have saved another $12 million and moved most high schools to 8 a.m. or later was dropped after strong community opposition because 85% of schools' times would change.

children.name: Transportation
children.blurb: Transportation in this chapter is the use of optimization tools to plan bus routes and, when districts choose, to adjust bell times alongside routing.

children.name: Scheduling and Staffing
children.blurb: Scheduling and staffing is the work of fitting student course requests, teacher assignments, room availability and required courses into a master timetable, and of filling teaching gaps when staff are absent.

children.name: Food Service
children.blurb: This idea is about using nutrition management software and AI to forecast meal demand, check menus against allergies and dietary needs, and help draft menus that meet federal nutrition requirements.

children.name: Operations Data and Privacy
children.blurb: Operations data and privacy is the idea that the systems schools use for buses, meals, and health information hold sensitive student data and need the same privacy protections as classroom tools.

children.name: Emergency Operations
children.blurb: Emergency operations in a school district means using forecasting tools to see problems coming, such as a storm that could make roads unsafe, while the decision to close or delay school stays with the superintendent or a designated leader.

children.name: Facilities and Energy
children.blurb: Facilities and energy management in schools can use AI to predict equipment failures, sort work orders by urgency, adjust building systems for occupancy, and handle routine rental questions.

children.name: Budget and Enrollment Forecasting
children.blurb: Budget and enrollment forecasting uses models to predict how many students will enroll in each school and grade, because funding often follows students.

children.name: Grants
children.blurb: Grants can bring significant resources to schools, but finding them and writing applications takes staff time.

children.name: Purchasing and Business Operations
children.blurb: This idea covers how schools use automation in purchasing and business operations.

children.name: Technology Operations
children.blurb: Technology operations in a school district covers the everyday systems that keep devices, networks, and data working.

children.name: Records, Minutes, and Policy
children.blurb: This idea covers how AI assisted search and transcription can support public records requests, board minutes, and policy lookup while keeping people responsible for review and release.

children.name: Safety Technology
children.blurb: Safety technology in schools includes AI security products such as camera analytics and weapon detection.

children.name: Cybersecurity Beyond Phishing
children.blurb: Cybersecurity beyond phishing means protecting schools from attacks such as ransomware that can close schools for days and expose student data.

children.name: The Staff Who Do the Work
children.blurb: This idea says that the people who run buses, cafeterias, buildings, and offices hold practical knowledge that data alone does not capture, and that this knowledge should shape how new tools are used.

children.name: Operations in the District AI Policy
children.blurb: A district AI policy should cover operations tools, not only classroom tools, because buses, meals and similar services make decisions that affect students every day.

children.name: How to Read a Savings Claim
children.blurb: How to read a savings claim is the practice of separating a verified saving from a vendor promise.

sections.body: Operations, facilities, transportation, and finance are the parts of school life that keep buildings open, buses running, meals served, staff scheduled, and money moving. The book says AI can save the most money here because transportation, food service, facilities, energy, scheduling, and business offices all involve complex problems where optimization and forecasting help. The clearest example is Boston Public Schools, where an optimization system redesigned bus routes, saved about $5 million a year, and removed 50 buses while keeping service quality. The same researchers proposed changing school start times, which would have saved another $12 million and moved most high schools to 8 a.m. or later. The chapter also covers technology operations, records and governance, and how to judge claims of savings, and it notes that the evidence base is thin, with only bus routing backed by published research from real districts.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: What works is the routing work that produced verified savings without lowering service quality. What does not work is an optimized plan that ignores people, as the start time plan failed after families objected strongly even though the math was sound. The book's rule is that tools can find better answers, and people must decide whether those answers fit the community. It also holds that operations savings must be real and fairly shared, so a district should verify savings and ask who bears any costs. The common failure pattern is announcing an efficient routing or scheduling change without involving families, then abandoning the plan and damaging trust, and the Thirty Day Move asks a district to apply the questions in Figure 19.4 to its largest operations tool, verify every fact in a grant application, and involve families from the start for changes that affect them.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages on Transportation, Scheduling and Staffing, and Food Service sit closest to the daily operations the chapter describes, and a leader would go to them for routing, staff schedules, and meal service questions. Facilities and Energy, Budget and Enrollment Forecasting, and Grants connect the money side, with facilities and energy for building use, forecasting for planning, and grants for the rule that every fact is verified before submission. Purchasing and Business Operations, Technology Operations, Records, Minutes, and Policy, and Cybersecurity Beyond Phishing cover the business and governance work, from buying and technology systems to records, policy, and security beyond basic phishing. Operations Data and Privacy, Emergency Operations, and Safety Technology address the risks and protections around operations data, emergencies, and safety tools, while The Staff Who Do the Work and Operations in the District AI Policy focus on the people doing the work and how the district policy should treat operations. How to Read a Savings Claim is the page a board member or parent would use to test whether promised savings are real and fairly shared, and it ties back to the savings report and the questions in Figure 19.4.
